meta.name: RPSGT Population and Protocol Boundaries Pack 1
meta.sourceBasis: Built from the uploaded 2024 AASM pediatric MSLT protocol paper and the uploaded Polysomnography for the Sleep Technologist reference. No proprietary scoring-manual rule table or figure is reproduced.
meta.clinicalBoundary: Educational protocol-boundary practice only. Current official AASM guidance, the interpreting clinician, facility policy, and supervised competency remain authoritative.
apaReferences: Maski, K. P., Amos, L. B., Carter, J. C., Koch, E. E., Kazmi, U., & Rosen, C. L. (2024). Recommended protocols for the Multiple Sleep Latency Test and Maintenance of Wakefulness Test in children: Guidance from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine. Journal of Clinical Sleep Medicine, 20(4), 631–641.
Robertson, B., Marshall, B., & Carno, M. A. (2014). Polysomnography for the sleep technologist. Elsevier.

cases.title: Adolescent MSLT after an abbreviated PSG night

profile.context: 8 h time in bed · 6 h 20 min total sleep time

cases.answer: Protocol boundary — routine pediatric MSLT conditions are not met; notify the sleep clinician and consider rescheduling.
cases.rationale: The 2024 pediatric AASM protocol states that the MSLT should follow an attended PSG allowing at least 8 hours of time in bed with at least 7 hours of total sleep time, ideally while meeting age-based sleep needs. The preceding PSG here does not reach the minimum total sleep time.

evidence.answer: The preceding PSG provided less than 7 hours of total sleep time, so the minimum pediatric PSG–MSLT preparation condition was not met.
options: The preceding PSG provided less than 7 hours of total sleep time, so the minimum pediatric PSG–MSLT preparation condition was not met.
Eight hours in bed automatically makes the MSLT valid regardless of actual sleep time.
The MSLT should always proceed because daytime sleepiness is the reason for testing.
Only adult MSLT protocols require review of prior-night sleep.

cases.title: MSLT scheduled after split-night PAP titration

profile.context: PAP pressures adjusted during the preceding night

cases.answer: Protocol boundary — do not perform the MSLT as a routine next-day study after a split-night or initial PAP titration night.
cases.rationale: The 2024 pediatric AASM protocol says the MSLT should not be performed after a night during which PAP pressures were adjusted, including a split-night or initial PAP titration study.

evidence.answer: PAP pressures were adjusted during the preceding night, which the pediatric protocol identifies as an inappropriate lead-in night for routine MSLT testing.
options: PAP pressures were adjusted during the preceding night, which the pediatric protocol identifies as an inappropriate lead-in night for routine MSLT testing.
A split-night study is preferred because it makes the patient more tired for the MSLT.
PAP titration has no potential effect on a next-day MSLT protocol.
The only requirement is that five nap opportunities can be scheduled.

cases.title: Very young child referred for MSLT

profile.context: Classic hypersomnolence symptoms; clinician evaluating narcolepsy

cases.answer: Population boundary — routine normative interpretation is limited under age 5; proceed only through clinician-directed special-circumstance planning.
cases.rationale: The 2024 pediatric protocol notes that MSLT may not be appropriate in children younger than 5 because normative data are lacking, while allowing that special circumstances may justify testing. This is a clinician-level decision rather than a technologist applying routine age assumptions.

evidence.answer: Normative pediatric MSLT data are limited below age 5, so the case requires special clinician-directed consideration rather than routine interpretation.
options: Normative pediatric MSLT data are limited below age 5, so the case requires special clinician-directed consideration rather than routine interpretation.
Adult MSLT normative assumptions should be applied because the recording montage is similar.
Any child younger than 5 is absolutely prohibited from undergoing MSLT under all circumstances.
Age does not affect MSLT planning or interpretation.

cases.title: Maintenance of Wakefulness Test requested for a teenager

profile.context: Treatment-response question; facility occasionally performs pediatric MWT

cases.answer: Evidence boundary — do not present pediatric MWT as a standardized validated protocol; involve the sleep clinician and document the limitation.
cases.rationale: The 2024 AASM pediatric paper reports no normative MWT values for people younger than 18 and insufficient data to develop a recommended pediatric MWT protocol, although some centers use the test clinically.

evidence.answer: The current pediatric AASM paper identifies no normative MWT values for patients under 18 and does not provide a recommended pediatric MWT protocol.
options: The current pediatric AASM paper identifies no normative MWT values for patients under 18 and does not provide a recommended pediatric MWT protocol.
The adult MWT protocol is automatically validated for every pediatric patient.
MWT is never used in any pediatric sleep center.
A pediatric MWT is interpreted only from the number of REM periods.

cases.title: Neurodevelopmental needs change how instructions are delivered

profile.context: Patient cannot reliably follow standard adult-style biocalibration wording

cases.answer: Protocol modification — tailor instructions to developmental age and document clinician-approved accommodations rather than forcing adult wording.
cases.rationale: The pediatric protocol specifically says biocalibration instructions should be tailored to developmental age and supports shared decision-making about protocol modifications for children and adolescents with neurodevelopmental or neurologic disorders, young age, or delayed sleep phase.

evidence.answer: Developmental-age tailoring and documented protocol modifications are explicitly contemplated in the pediatric guidance.
options: Developmental-age tailoring and documented protocol modifications are explicitly contemplated in the pediatric guidance.
Every instruction must be delivered word-for-word using adult phrasing or the entire study is automatically invalid.
The technologist should omit biocalibrations without documenting the change.
Parents or caregivers should independently change the protocol without clinician involvement.

cases.title: Old local worksheet conflicts with current guidance

profile.context: Facility worksheet is dated; current official guidance may have changed

cases.answer: Source-hierarchy boundary — stop, verify current official guidance and the facility’s current approved protocol, then document the resolution.
cases.rationale: Sleep technologists are expected to apply professionally accepted guidance, follow center-specific protocols, and comply with applicable standards. A stale worksheet should not silently override current official guidance or an updated facility policy.

evidence.answer: The safe response is to verify the current authoritative rule and current facility protocol rather than relying on a dated local worksheet from memory.
options: The safe response is to verify the current authoritative rule and current facility protocol rather than relying on a dated local worksheet from memory.
The oldest local worksheet always overrides newer professional guidance.
The technologist should invent a compromise rule between the two sources.
Protocol conflicts should be ignored if the waveform looks familiar.
